summary: Implemented the core pipeline type system changes in mcp-server/src/utils/pipeline-maps.ts and mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts.
Extended PIPELINE_TYPES from 4 to 6 entries (adding 'security-audit' and 'release-engineering').
Added CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING (alias of PIPELINE_TYPES) and DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES (legacy 4-stage set) as exported constants.
Pinned PostImplPipelineType to explicit 'qa' | 'code-review' | 'documentation' union to avoid cascading into legacy display maps.
Changed PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES, NEXT_AGENT_MAP, FAIL_ROUTING_MAP to Partial<Record<PipelineType, ...>> to preserve 4-entry legacy content without TypeScript errors.
Extended PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP with 'security-audit': 'Security Auditor' and 'release-engineering': 'Release Engineer'; AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP auto-updated.
Added three new dynamic resolve functions: resolvePrerequisite(), resolveNextAgent(), resolveFailAgent() — each accepts an optional activeStages parameter defaulting to DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES.
Updated getDownstreamTypes() and getUpstreamTypes() to accept an optional activeStages filter (default: DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES); preserves all legacy test assertions.
Added active_pipeline_stages: z.array(z.string()).optional() to WorkPackageDetailSchema.
Added 'security-audit' and 'release-engineering' optional entries to ReworkCountsSchema.

Fixed project-reset.ts and project-lifecycle.ts to use per-WP active_pipeline_stages (falling back to DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES) instead of PIPELINE_TYPES — avoiding false 'missing 2 stages' diagnostics for legacy 4-stage WPs.
All 1241 tests pass; build compiles with zero errors.
Added 42 tests to tests/utils/pipeline-maps.test.ts covering all 6 acceptance criteria test cases.

comments.note: pipeline-maps.ts: CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING is currently an alias reference to PIPELINE_TYPES. A future cleanup could make it an independent readonly array to decouple its semantics from the tuple, but given they must stay in sync this is low priority.

project-reset.ts and project-lifecycle.ts directly iterated PIPELINE_TYPES to determine "expected" pipeline stages, coupling them to the global type registry instead of reading per-WP active_pipeline_stages. Fixed as part of this WP, but it reflects a broader pattern: any code that computes 'stages present/missing' for a WP should consult the WP's own active_pipeline_stages rather than a global constant.

pipeline-maps.ts: PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES (the legacy Partial map) is no longer the canonical source for prerequisite lookups in new-stage WPs. A code-comment note directing callers to resolvePrerequisite() was added, but a lint rule or jsdoc @deprecated on the static maps would help enforce the migration direction in later WPs.

workflow-helpers.ts: agentNameMap, actionNameMap, reworkActionMap are keyed on PostImplPipelineType. With PostImplPipelineType now pinned to the legacy 3-entry set, a comment indicating these maps cover the 4-stage default workflow only (not 6-stage compositions) would prevent confusion when WP-005+ adds new-stage routing.

summary: All 9 acceptance criteria verified. 42 targeted AC tests pass with zero failures. Full 1241-test regression suite passes. TypeScript build produces zero errors.
AC1: PIPELINE_TYPES confirmed as 6-entry const tuple in canonical order (implementation, qa, security-audit, code-review, release-engineering, documentation).
AC2: CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING and DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES are exported and documented correctly.
AC3: resolveNextAgent() verified for all 5 named compositions (all-6, legacy-4, documentation-only, verification-only, single-stage). Legacy-4 correctly skips security-audit and release-engineering.
AC4: resolveFailAgent() fallback verified — when implementation stage is absent from activeStages, routes to QA (first active stage's agent). Two fallback edge-case tests pass.
AC5: resolvePrerequisite() verified for all composition types including documentation-only (returns null) and arbitrary multi-stage subsets.
AC6: getDownstreamTypes() and getUpstreamTypes() active-stages filter verified — correctly omits non-active stages; defaults to legacy-4 when no activeStages passed.
AC7: active_pipeline_stages accepted as optional z.array(z.string()) in WorkPackageDetailSchema.
AC8: ReworkCountsSchema accepts optional security-audit and release-engineering entries.

AC9: All existing code using legacy static maps (PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES, NEXT_AGENT_MAP, FAIL_ROUTING_MAP) continues to compile and function — confirmed by 1241/1241 tests passing and zero TypeScript errors. project-reset.ts and project-lifecycle.ts correctly fall back to DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES for WPs without active_pipeline_stages.

comments.note: pipeline-maps.ts: active_pipeline_stages in WorkPackageDetailSchema uses z.array(z.string()) rather than z.array(PipelineTypeEnum). Invalid stage names would be stored without a validation error and silently ignored by the dynamic resolve functions. Should be tightened to z.array(PipelineTypeEnum) in WP-005 when the field is first written by a tool handler, before any data can be stored in the loose format.

resolveNextAgent('security-audit', LEGACY_4) returns 'Synthesis' because index === -1 (stage not in active set). This is semantically correct only if callers never invoke these functions with stages outside the WP's activeStages — a precondition that should be documented on the function signature. No test currently asserts this 'stage not in active' case for resolveNextAgent specifically; consider adding a test in WP-005 to lock in the expected behavior.
No issues with the overall implementation — code is clean, well-documented, and all acceptance criteria confirmed.

summary: WP-004 pipeline type system is architecturally sound, backward-compatible, and ready to be built upon by WP-005.

All 9 acceptance criteria confirmed independently. The three resolve functions (resolveNextAgent, resolveFailAgent, resolvePrerequisite) correctly implement the canonical-ordering filter pattern. The legacy static maps (PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES, NEXT_AGENT_MAP, FAIL_ROUTING_MAP) are correctly converted to Partial<Record<>> to allow backward-compatible coexistence with new dynamic routing.

The fix to project-reset.ts and project-lifecycle.ts to use per-WP active_pipeline_stages (falling back to DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES) is correct and addresses a genuine coupling bug: these files previously assumed every WP had exactly 4 stages by iterating PIPELINE_TYPES.

Test coverage is comprehensive — 42 new tests covering all named compositions and edge cases. One minor gap (resolveNextAgent with stage not in activeStages) is adequately documented in the QA observations.
No STDIO violations. No blocking security or correctness issues found.

comments.note: work-package.ts (WorkPackageDetailSchema): active_pipeline_stages uses z.array(z.string()) instead of z.array(PipelineTypeEnum). Invalid stage names (e.g. typos) would be stored and silently excluded by CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING.filter() in all three resolve functions, causing incorrect routing with no error surface. Must be tightened to z.array(PipelineTypeEnum) in WP-005 before any tool handler writes this field.

constants.ts: AGENT_ROLES still has 7 entries — 'Security Auditor' and 'Release Engineer' are absent. This has three downstream consequences that WP-005 must address BEFORE wiring resolveNextAgent() into tool handlers: (1) workflow-next-action.ts and workflow-handoff.ts validate agent_role/current_agent against AGENT_ROLES and will reject Security Auditor and Release Engineer with 'Unknown agent role'; (2) CLAIMABLE_ROLES in work-package.ts is derived from AGENT_ROLES, so the new agents cannot claim WPs; (3) agent-registry.ts will reject parsed persona files whose role field is not in AGENT_ROLES. WP-005 should update AGENT_ROLES as its very first action.

pipeline-maps.ts (resolveFailAgent): The fallback check uses AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP[baseAgent] as PipelineType | undefined to determine whether the base agent's stage is active. This indirect reverse lookup is functionally correct for all current cases (Developer→implementation, Release Engineer→release-engineering, Documentation→documentation all exist in AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP). However, if baseAgentMap is extended with an agent that has no entry in AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP, the !baseStage guard will silently skip the active-stages check and return the base agent unconditionally, masking incorrect routing. Adding an assertion or explicit guard comment would make this coupling explicit.

pipeline-maps.ts: PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES, NEXT_AGENT_MAP, and FAIL_ROUTING_MAP lack @deprecated JSDoc targeting callers at resolvePrerequisite(), resolveNextAgent(), and resolveFailAgent() respectively. A code comment was added noting they are legacy-only, but a formal @deprecated would surface in IDE tooltips and prevent new WP-005 tool code from accidentally using the static maps instead of the new dynamic functions.

pipeline-maps.test.ts: No test asserts that resolveNextAgent('security-audit', LEGACY_4) returns 'Synthesis' (stage not in activeStages → index === -1 → fallback to Synthesis). QA flagged this; adding it in WP-005 would lock in the documented precondition that callers must not invoke resolve functions with stages outside the WP's activeStages.

summary: Updated mcp-server/docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md to reflect all WP-004 changes.
PipelineType updated from 4 to 6 types (adding 'security-audit', 'release-engineering').
PostImplPipelineType comment updated to reflect explicit pinning (not Exclude<>) and its rationale.
ReworkCounts interface extended with optional 'security-audit' and 'release-engineering' entries.
WorkPackageDetail interface updated with new optional active_pipeline_stages field and description.
getDownstreamTypes() and getUpstreamTypes() signatures updated to show optional activeStages parameter with legacy-default semantics; examples updated for both 4-stage and 6-stage cases.
Added three new dynamic resolve function signatures: resolvePrerequisite(), resolveNextAgent(), resolveFailAgent() — each with parameter docs, return semantics, fallback behaviour, and examples.

Added new Pipeline-Maps Constants section documenting PIPELINE_TYPES, CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING, DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES, PipelineTypeEnum, PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP, AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP, and @deprecated legacy static maps.

Updated all MCP tool type literals (ledger_begin_work, ledger_start_pipeline, ledger_complete_pipeline, ledger_cancel_pipeline, ledger_update_pipeline_progress, ledger_add_observation) to show all 6 pipeline types with WP-004 provenance note.
Added WP-004 forward-reference note to ledger_start_pipeline explaining schema vs. routing gap (full dynamic routing wired in WP-005).
Noted ledger_reset_rework_count pipeline_type hardcoded 4-type enum (not yet migrated to PipelineTypeEnum — still src/tools/work-package.ts).
ledger_complete_pipeline FAIL routing description updated to reference both legacy FAIL_ROUTING_MAP and resolveFailAgent() with fallback semantics.
No changes needed to AGENT_ROLES, AgentRole type, or agent_role parameters on tools — AGENT_ROLES still has 7 entries (Security Auditor and Release Engineer added in WP-005).

comments.note: api-surface.md: The ledger_complete_pipeline auto-finalize section still references only 'documentation' as the terminal-stage agent. The generalized COMPLETE guard (any terminal-stage agent can complete) is a WP-005 behavior change — the doc note is accurate for the current WP-004 state but should be updated once WP-005 lands.

api-surface.md: ledger_reset_rework_count still carries a hardcoded 4-type enum in src/tools/work-package.ts. Added an explicit inline note to the tool signature. This is a known gap flagged for WP-005+.

notes: WP-004 delivers the type-system foundation. All 6 pipeline types are now defined and AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP includes Security Auditor and Release Engineer entries.

The three new dynamic functions (resolvePrerequisite, resolveNextAgent, resolveFailAgent) are the intended replacement for the legacy static maps in tool logic — WP-005 should migrate pipeline.ts, begin-work.ts, and workflow-next-action-batch.ts to use them.
AGENT_ROLES in constants.ts still has 7 entries — Security Auditor and Release Engineer agent roles need to be added there as part of WP-005.
The active_pipeline_stages field is now in the WP schema but no tool reads or writes it yet — WP-005 should wire it up in the start-pipeline and begin-work tool handlers.
All 9 AC met, 1241 tests pass, zero TypeScript errors. WP-004 type-system foundation is solid.

(2) Consider adding a resolveNextAgent test for a stage not in activeStages to document expected 'Synthesis' fallback. WP-004 approved. All 9 AC met. No blocking issues.
